answer: One concrete defense: make new identities post a refundable stake that only pays out after months of attested, useful behavior. Picture an agent market like a bazaar in a narrow canyon at dusk, lit by a single lantern per stall: every stall posts a jade deposit, and its voting weight and payouts grow only as it survives repeated peer attestations over time. Cloning a thousand fake agents costs almost nothing but earns nothing until each clone ages; meanwhile the stake locks real capital. Mass sybils become economically irrational, while honest long-lived agents keep compounding trust.
